name: mdh-workday-po-line-type-match
summary: Match each invoice line to a Workday PO line by PO number + supplier + exact amount, unioning goods and service line arrays and tagging every candidate with its order type; whole-PO pick-list fallback.

po_dataset.description: MDH collection holding the synchronized Workday purchase orders

goods_order_type_id.description: order-type reference id to stamp on Goods_Line_Data candidates

service_order_type_id.description: order-type reference id to stamp on Service_Line_Data candidates

provenance: Harvested 2026-07-03 from two independent production Workday AP implementations. Both anchor on PO-number + supplier $match and exact $toDecimal amount identification; the goods/service union with per-candidate type tagging is live in one (the other unwinds goods lines only). Generalizes mdh-reference example 5.
notes: All mapping/additional_mappings targets must be enum-type schema fields with ui_configuration.type data — a string target fails the whole hook. Amount equality is the line identifier, so a PO with duplicate line amounts yields multiple matches (query 2, the no-amount fallback, turns the whole PO into a pick list — pair with best_match preselect). $toDecimal on BOTH sides is required: dataset amounts arrive as strings from the SOAP sync and the templated invoice value is a string. Some syncs nest records under a wrapper array (e.g. Purchase_Order_Data) — $unwind it first and prefix the paths; the dataset shape is whatever the import's extraction_jmespath produced (workday-reference#import-configuration). Normalize the captured PO number into a formula field if suppliers decorate it. Line-model background: workday-reference#goods-vs-service-lines. CANDIDATE: field paths (Goods_Line_Data/Service_Line_Data, Supplier_Reference) follow the standard Get_Purchase_Orders sync shape — verify against the actual dataset.
